newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on profit taking.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained sharply lower late Tuesday in fairly active trade, pressured the entire session by profit taking after Monday's 17 percent, weather-related rally, industry sources said.
At 1430 EST, February was still down by 31.6 cents at $3.32 per million British thermal units. March was 22.5 cents lower at $2.98. Most others were off by two to 12 cents.

"I think the move yesterday was exaggerated and this is a retracement back to reality," said one East Coast buyer, noting prices rallied sharply recently on forecasts for much colder weather this week.
Forecasters expected well below-normal temperatures to dominate the Midwest and East over the next week, but the western half of the nation was expected to moderate by midmonth.
Early withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's AGA report range from 45 bcf to 120 bcf versus last year's decline of 138 bcf.

Technically, traders now pegged February resistance in the $3.80-3.84 area, then in the $3.90s and then at the contract high of $4.02. Support remained in the gap at $3.11-3.28 and then in the $2.60s.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices jumped Tuesday by more than 30 cents to the high-$3.70s. Midcon pipes were 20 cents higher in the mid-to-high $3.80s. New York city gate gas gained another 50 cents to about $4.50.
NYMEX said 38,745 Hub contracts traded at 1355 EST.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1145 EST.
On the KCBT, February skidded 26 cents to $3.24, while deferreds were steady to down 10 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 5.6 cents to eight cents (NYMEX premium).
